primary_contexts.finding: Implication introduction preserves the antecedent in its conditional conclusion.
Cont adds unique codes; its own proof explicitly allows Pow code sets to be larger when codes repeat.

counterexamples.construction: Let Gamma be empty and A=B=P. The assumption P entails P, but the empty context does not entail P (take P false). Implication introduction yields P -> P, matching the frozen N2 introduction rule.

Take D=N disjoint-union P(N) disjoint-union P(P(N)), X the N component and Y=D. Each member of the P(N) component codes its corresponding subset of X; all other domain members code the empty subset. Pow(Y,R,X) holds, with many repeated empty-set codes, but |Y| >= |P(P(N))| > |P(N)| = continuum. Adding the source Cont uniqueness clause gives a bijection Y -> P(X).
counterexamples.exact_original_text: set~$Y$ that codes the power set of set~$X$ of size~$\aleph_0$.
counterexamples.exact_proposed_source_text: set~$Y$ that codes the power set of set~$X$ of size~$\aleph_0$, with distinct elements of~$Y$ coding distinct subsets of~$X$.
